studies.Title: The association of plasma fatty acids with prostate cancer risk in Nigerians.
studies.Reference: The association of plasma fatty acids with prostate cancer risk in Nigerians.
studies.Population: Men aged 40 years or older recruited from clinics and rural and urban communities
studies.comparison_type: second versus first plasma fatty-acid quartile

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Mean ages for 66 (22.6%) cases and 226 (77.4%) controls were 71.9+/-11.47 and 56.7+/-12.69 years, P<.001, and median (25th, 75th percentile) fasting plasma FA were 2,447 (2,087, 3,024) and 2,373 (2,014, 2,751) microg/mL, respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Mean ages for 66 (22.6%) cases and 226 (77.4%) controls were 71.9+/-11.47 and 56.7+/-12.69 years, P<.001, and median (25th, 75th percentile) fasting plasma FA were 2,447 (2,087, 3,024) and 2,373 (2,014, 2,751) microg/mL, respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Unadjusted ORQ2vs.Q1 for omega-3 FAs eicosapentaenoic (EPA) and docosapentaenoic (DPA) were 0.39 (95% CI, 0.18-0.85) and 0.79 (95% CI, 0.35-1.79) respectively. In this population with high total plasma omega-3, we observed modest positive PCa risk trend with total plasma omega-6 (2.3), inverse risk reduction with EPA (0.4), and strong positive risk associations with behenic (2.8), erucic (4.2), and nervonic (2.4) acids.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Unadjusted ORQ2vs.Q1 for omega-3 FAs eicosapentaenoic (EPA) and docosapentaenoic (DPA) were 0.39 (95% CI, 0.18-0.85) and 0.79 (95% CI, 0.35-1.79) respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: ORQ2vs.Q1 for omega-3 FAs eicosapentaenoic (EPA) and docosapentaenoic (DPA)
extraction_supporting_text.design: Odds ratio (OR) of PCa risk was determined by unconditional logistic regression with the plasma FA 1st quartile as reference
extraction_supporting_text.timing: 30 mLs of fasting blood collected for prostatic specific antigen and fatty acid (FA) analysis.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: 30 mLs of fasting blood collected for prostatic specific antigen and fatty acid (FA) analysis.
